column4: Visit note | 2025-06-30 12:30 PM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Abul Chowdhury, 28, male. Mr. Chowdhury visits us today because he is troubled by an itchy skin rash that seems to have spreading edges, with the itchiness becoming much worse whenever the weather is particularly humid. He is a CNG auto-rickshaw driver and mentions that the problem first began during the humid monsoon in Old Dhaka while he was sweating profusely behind the wheel. He notes that the itching disturbs his sleep and makes long driving shifts uncomfortable. Apart from the rash, he has a known history of Bronchial asthma which is currently stable, though he reports no recent shortness of breath or wheezing. He denies any recent fever, joint pain, blisters, or involvement of his face or scalp. On physical examination today, his vital signs and measurements are as follows: affected area about 4 cm across, BP 110/85 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 68 kg. The skin lesion on his trunk shows an annular, erythematous, scaly plaque with central clearing and well-defined raised margins. There is no secondary bacterial infection, weeping, or significant lymphadenopathy observed. Systemic examination reveals clear lung fields with normal vesicular breath sounds and no wheezes. Based on the clinical presentation and physical findings, our evaluation confirms the condition. Assessment: Tinea corporis. To manage this skin condition effectively, a prescription was issued today containing targeted antifungal agents and soothing preparations. He was instructed to keep the skin dry, avoid sharing towels with family members, and wash all personal clothes and linens in hot water to prevent reinfection. Follow-up is recommended in 2 weeks to assess treatment response and healing progress.
